correctness.rationale: For all primes r>7 and positive a,b,c, the exact logarithmic derivative and totient identities reduce equality to (24−7a−5b)r=35c+24. Positivity leaves only (a,b)=(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,1); modular 7 and 5 exclude the middle and last. The other two yield respectively r≡2 mod35 with c=(12r−24)/35, and r≡12 mod35 with c=(2r−24)/35; minimum primes 37 and 47 give c>0. Both residues coprime to 35, so Dirichlet proves infinitely many primes. Our independent integer enumeration over all 58 primes 7<r<300 obtained exactly the four predicted qualifying supports; this is corroboration, not the infinite proof.
